system_instruction:
You write a short evidence brief on the lung cancer care pathway for one Finnish wellbeing services county, for the county's health managers. You may use ONLY the claims provided. Each claim has an ID, a status and a text.

Rules:
1. Every sentence must list the IDs of the claims it relies on in claim_ids (at least one). Use IDs exactly as given. Do not cite anything that is not in the list.
2. Copy every number exactly as it appears in a cited claim, at the same precision. Do NOT calculate new numbers (no differences, ratios or percentage-point gaps): state the county value and the national value side by side instead. Spell out no numbers in words.
3. State uncertainty. Give 95% confidence intervals where the claim has one. Say that the county shares are crude (not adjusted for age or stage). Where an age-adjusted value exists (Kuva 16, digitised from a figure, about ±0.5 percentage points), use it to say whether a gap holds after age adjustment, and say it is digitised.
4. The treatment categories overlap (a patient can have several); never add them up or present them as a breakdown. "No treatment record within 12 months" mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded; never call it "untreated" or "missing data". MDT records measure recording practice, not care.
5. Label status in the sentence itself: a sentence citing a claim with status "preliminary" must say "preliminary" (e.g. "preliminary, unpublished figures"); one citing "mentor insight" must say "mentor insight". Claims "verified by Hellu" come from a teammate's reading of regional documents.
6. "where_we_lag": where this county's pathway lags national values (3–5 sentences). "how_sure_are_we": what is certain, what is uncertain and what public data cannot show (3–5 sentences). "what_to_do_first": the first steps, drawn from the team's draft recommendations and suited to this county's data, each backed by evidence claims (2–4 sentences).
7. Plain, direct English. No claims about other counties. No headings or numbering inside sentences.

## THE TEAM'S DRAFT RECOMMENDATIONS (context only; cite the evidence claims, not these)
1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts
each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's *Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa* (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.

2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact
- Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. - Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. - Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.

3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.

where_we_lag.text: In Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue, the crude share of new lung cancer patients in 2019–2023 who received curative treatment was 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7; n=114/591), which lags the national figure of 27.0% in Taulukko 11 and 26.9% (4009/14873) in Taulukko 6.

In age-adjusted figures digitised from Kuva 16, the curative treatment gap holds for men in Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue at 17.9% (95% CI 13.9–22.9) compared with the national reference line of 26.7%, while for women the age-adjusted share is 22.6% (95% CI 16.8–29.3) compared with 26.9% nationally, with the 95% confidence interval for women overlapping the national value.

Alongside lower curative treatment, the county's crude shares are above national levels for life-prolonging treatment at 37.6% (95% CI 33.8–41.5; n=222/591) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally and for symptomatic treatment at 51.3% (95% CI 47.2–55.3; n=303/591) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) nationally, though these treatment categories overlap because a patient can receive several treatments within the follow-up period.

Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue also lags in recorded multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings at a crude share of 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=3/591) compared with 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, although MDT records reflect HILMO recording practices from direct patient contacts rather than actual multidisciplinary care.

how_sure_are_we.text: It is certain from the 95% confidence intervals that Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue's crude curative share of 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7; n=114/591) vs 27.0% nationally and digitised age-adjusted curative share for men of 17.9% (95% CI 13.9–22.9) vs 26.7% nationally are below national benchmarks, whereas the digitised age-adjusted curative share for women of 22.6% (95% CI 16.8–29.3) vs 26.9% nationally has a wide confidence interval that leaves an age-adjusted gap for women uncertain.

All county treatment shares in Taulukko 11 are crude and unadjusted for age or stage, and case-mix interpretation remains uncertain because stage at diagnosis is missing for a large share of new patients and the reporting, collection, and storage of lung cancer data in Finland are currently incomplete.

Furthermore, the crude share of patients with no treatment record within 12 months is 16.4% (95% CI 13.7–19.6; n=97/591) in Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue compared with 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, which creates uncertainty because this category mixes patients who were not treated with patients whose treatment was not recorded.

Public data cannot show where pathway bottlenecks occur in the county because symptoms, referrals, and outpatient primary care or occupational health visits are not measured, first specialist visits are not reported by county, and county treatment start data show treatment type only, even though preliminary, unpublished figures for Finland show an average of 155 days from first symptoms to treatment (compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark), divided into 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

what_to_do_first.text: Because Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue has a lower crude curative share of 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7; n=114/591) vs 27.0% nationally, preliminary figures identify specialist care as the longest delay stage at 58 days, and a teammate's reading of regional documents notes that there is no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion, the county should start tracking and reporting lung cancer access times across referral, specialist assessment, diagnosis, and treatment start using THL (Ohjaus 21/2016) definitions to flag stalled handovers.

Drawing on mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care and that occupational health gets patients to specialist care faster, together with practices identified from a teammate's reading of regional documents and national pathway goals, the county should adopt standardised referral criteria with a mandatory referral template, instruct primary care to refer patients with persistent unexplained symptoms for a pulmonologist assessment even when an X-ray is clear, and assign a named contact person to coordinate care during the diagnostic phase.

Finally, to address the county's 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=3/591) recorded MDT rate versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, its 16.4% (95% CI 13.7–19.6; n=97/591) share with no treatment record within 12 months versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, and missing stage data, Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue should audit and report the completeness of stage, treatment, and MDT coding using uniform recording instructions in preparation for the planned national cancer quality registry and its 90% data coverage target.
